content: Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.
author: Swami Vivekananda
sourceWork: Katha Upanishad / Lectures from Colombo to Almora
explanation:
Derived from the ancient Katha Upanishad, Vivekananda transformed this ancient Sanskrit invocation into an urgent clarion call for modern human dignity. It is not a gentle suggestion to try your best; it is an uncompromising demand to shake off the hypnotic slumber of self-doubt, victimhood, and procrastination. When you recognize that inner weakness is an illusion born of conditioning, hesitation ceases to have power over you.

The human spirit was not engineered for half-hearted compromise. The moment you define your worthy purpose, every ounce of nervous energy must be directed toward it until the summit is won.
practicalInsight: Identify the one critical objective you have been treating with hesitant, half-hearted steps. Make an unequivocal commitment today to pursue it with complete, undivided effort.
reflectionPrompt: What goal have you allowed to drift into complacency, and what bold action would prove you are truly awake to it?
